title: Snake Now Playable Without a Keyboard
body:
By Res Londres

Snake can now be played without a keyboard after an on-screen directional controller was added to the game today, allowing the arcade remake to be played on touch screen devices for the first time.

The controller places four directional buttons in a cross shape below the canvas. Tapping any of them starts a round and steers the snake, exactly as the arrow keys do.

Under the hood, the four buttons each carry a direction label. A single click listener intercepts taps on any element with a direction attribute, translates the label into the equivalent keyboard code (37, 38, 39, and 40 for left, up, right, and down) and passes it to the same functions the arrow keys already called.

The game itself is otherwise unchanged. Food remains worth 10 points, the snake moves on a 15-pixel grid, and the canvas refreshes every 100 milliseconds. Keyboard support remains intact, and desktop players can still start a round with any arrow key.

Highscores continue to reset when the page reloads, a limitation that has not yet been addressed.
